Olivia (Acme Corp): Hi team — for the upcoming POC can we confirm we can keep all inference and embeddings traffic within the EU? Customer wants EU-only processing and wants BYOK for KMS.
Ava (Sales): short answer: yes, with either Dedicated or a Private deployment. There are tradeoffs on cost and failover. Do they need multi-AZ in eu-west? :thinking_face:
Olivia (Acme Corp): Ideally single-region EU (eu-central-1) for latency, but must not leave EU for data processing or fallthrough. Egress to third-party subprocessors is a blocker — need subproc list and certs.
Raj (SE): We can pin tenant to eu-central-1. Routing config example:```json
{"tenant_routing": {"region_hint": "eu-central-1", "strict_pin": true, "fallback": "no-fallback"}}
```If strict_pin=true, autoscaling is within that region only. That will affect burst capacity.
Liam (Solutions): For a POC we usually do: hosted eu-only control plane + dedicated compute in EU for inference. Pricing note: regional pin + BYOK = uplift vs standard hosted. Rough baseline: expect ~15–25% delta depending on instance sizing. I'll get a more concrete estimate once we know qps/token rates.
Maria (Security): On subprocessors — we have an EU-only subprocessors list PDF (SOC2 + EU DPA). I can attach the latest attestation in the handoff. BYOK KMS: we support customer-managed keys via KMS in EU regions; key material stays in customer KMS. Need to know if they require HSM-backed keys.
Olivia (Acme Corp): HSM preferred but not mandatory for POC. Also need to know if logs/traces can be excluded from export outside EU (no telemetry export).
Raj (SE): Logs/traces can be configured to retain in-customer VPC or pushed to customer SIEM in EU. By default we redact sensitive tokens; still need to capture audit logs for SLA.
Ava (Sales): Ken, can legal commit to a CFRA clause or subprocessor restriction for the POC? Customer asking for contract language around no-cross-border processing.
Ken (Legal): We can add a limited-scope addendum for the POC: restrict processing to EU region(s) and list approved subprocessors. Must align with privacy/data transfer policy. I need Maria's subprocessors list and Liam's deployment sketch.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary-eu-pin 1716008000 by ops-team — will not run unless signoff received.
Liam (Solutions): Next steps I propose: 1) Maria shares subprocessors PDF + attestation. 2) Raj produces a brief deployment plan (capacity, fallback behavior, costs). 3) Ken drafts POC addendum. 4) Ava shares ballpark pricing for EU-dedicated baseline. ETA: 48h for docs, 72h for formal quote.
Olivia (Acme Corp): Good. Two quick asks: 1) SLA when pinned (p99 latency objective?) 2) Any extra egress fees if we keep third-party integrations in EU?
Raj (SE): SLA depends on Dedicated vs Hosted pinned. Dedicated can have SLA-backed throughput/latency; hosted pinned is best-effort for latency but we can set SLOs. Exact numbers in the quote. Egress: if traffic stays in EU and subprocessors are EU-based, no cross-border egress charges from our side; cloud provider egress still applies for any outbound to customer endpoints outside region.
Ava (Sales): Olivia — I'll collect required Qs in a short checklist. Can you confirm expected qps, average tokens per request, and if they need realtime streaming? That affects instance size and cost.
Olivia (Acme Corp): Will send QPS + token profile today. Also looping in our security contact for KMS attestation. :+1:
Maria (Security): I'll upload subprocessors and the BYOK integration guide to the shared drive and @Ava when done.
Ken (Legal): Once I have the subprocessors list, I'll draft the limited POC addendum and send via Docusign for quick signature.
Ava (Sales): Perfect — I'll update the deal checklist and schedule a short sync with Olivia and Raj tomorrow. :calendar: 
Olivia (Acme Corp): Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick responses.
ops-bot: Note: any strict_pin=true deployment requires a dedicated capacity request. Ticket template: #dedicated-capacity-request — please include expected sustained qps and max burst.
